memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "When someone has a boil on their skin and it heals, and in the place where the boil was, a white swelling or reddish-white spot appears, they must present themselves to the priest. The priest is to examine it, and if it appears to be more than skin deep and the hair in it has turned white, the priest shall pronounce that person unclean. It is a defiling skin disease that has broken out where the boil was." - Lev 13:18-20 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Notice where the trouble appears: in the place where the boil was. The old injury had healed. And that healed place is precisely where something new broke out.

Anyone who has walked with God for a while knows this pattern. The area where we once struggled and were delivered is often exactly where the enemy returns. The temper we dealt with years ago. The relationship pattern we thought we had broken. The old insecurity that resurfaces in a new season.

It can be discouraging — as though the earlier work never counted. But that is not what this passage says. The earlier healing was real. This is a new outbreak in an old location, and it needs the same honest attention the first one received.

Paul told the Ephesians to put on the full armour of God so that they could stand their ground, and after they had done everything, to stand (Eph 6:13). Notice that last phrase. Even after everything, the standing continues. There is no point at which vigilance is retired.

Do not despair over old ground. Go back to the Priest. The same grace that healed you the first time has not diminished, and He is not exasperated with you for coming again.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where has an old struggle resurfaced in your life?
2. Do you feel discouraged by that, or ready to bring it back to God?
3. What safeguards could you put in place in that particular area?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, when old struggles return I am tempted to despair. Remind me that Your grace is not exhausted and that You welcome me back as gladly as the first time. Amen.
